case.title: Gotion's battery plants inside the US
case.subtitle: Gotion, Inc. and Gotion Illinois New Energy · Fremont, California and Manteno, Illinois, USA
case.question: When a Chinese-owned battery company builds its plant inside the US, can Sayari show both who owns it and the Chinese inputs going into it?
case.answer: Inputs, yes: Sayari shows dated shipments of Chinese cells, packs and one lot of artificial graphite from Gotion's own Chinese plants into its US companies. Ownership only in part: Chinese registry data traces Gotion High-Tech down to a US subsidiary, but no US record shows who owns the Fremont or Manteno companies.
case.why_it_matters: Since July 2025, US clean-energy tax credits depend on whether a company is owned or controlled by a 'prohibited foreign entity'. Here no third country is involved: the Chinese-owned plant is in Illinois, and its inputs come straight from the parent's factories in China. The paper trail is short, but the key ownership link sits in Chinese filings, not US ones.
case.headline: Partly. The trade side is clear: Gotion's Chinese plants ship cells, packs, parts and, once, artificial graphite to Gotion Inc. and its Manteno plant, Dec 2025 to Sep 2026. The ownership side is incomplete. Chinese records show Gotion High-Tech owning a US subsidiary through Hefei Gotion, but US registries list no shareholder, so the last link rests on name and press.
case.summary_for_non_experts: Gotion High-Tech is a Chinese battery maker based in Hefei. Its US arm, Gotion, Inc., is in Fremont, California, and runs a plant in Manteno, Illinois that assembles energy-storage systems and EV battery packs. US customs records show the inputs coming almost entirely from Gotion's own factories in China, including one lot of artificial graphite routed through Korea. Chinese filings show the parent owning a US subsidiary, but US registries don't say who owns the plant, and Gotion's planned Michigan plant was never built.

steps.title: The US companies: one name, many records
steps.text: Gotion, Inc. appears as a California registry record, a federal SAM record and several trade records at 48660 Kato Road, Fremont. The SAM record carries the California company number, so those two are one company. The Manteno plant has a SAM record and two trade records at 333 South Spruce Street. One trade record is wrongly typed as a person.

steps.title: The owner: visible from China, not from the US
steps.text: Chinese registry data shows Gotion High-Tech owning 99.8% of Hefei Gotion, which owns a 'Gotion High-Tech (USA)' company in China's outbound-investment filings. California lists no shareholders, and Sayari found no owners for Gotion, Inc. A director, Steven Cai, shares a name with a Gotion High-Tech director. Registry data also lists Volkswagen (China) Investment as a shareholder of the parent, with no percentage.

steps.title: Inputs: straight from the parent's factories
steps.text: Two rows of artificial graphite (HS 3801.10) went from Hefei Gotion to Gotion Inc. in Fremont, shipped from Busan on 23 Dec 2025. Lithium-ion cells and packs (HS 8507) arrive from Hefei Gotion and the group's Tongcheng plant, some via Jamaica. That includes 29 rows of packs bound for Manteno in Aug 2026. A Taiwan trader, Green Innovation International, sends pack covers and storage-system parts. No natural graphite (HS 2504) or petroleum coke appears.

steps.title: Customers and status
steps.text: US records don't show who buys from the Manteno plant; US export and domestic sales aren't in customs data. A press release names Richardson Electronics as a storage partner. Sayari does show US firms buying Gotion batteries straight from China, such as Moxion Power, up to Feb 2024. Manteno is operating, with five lines and about 300 staff by Nov 2025. Big Rapids, Michigan, was declared abandoned by the state in Sep 2025 and is now in court.

red_flags.flag: Volume spike after a policy date
red_flags.note: Rows cluster Jul–Sep 2026, but we read only a sample and can't separate a ramp-up from a policy effect.

red_flags.note: A director name shared with the parent; the parent's flags are adjacency flags on a stale record.
Seven US records, two parent records, a person-typed company and an ownership loop.
Sub-tier 'product blueprint' flags on the Gotion Inc. trade record; context, not a finding.

caveats: Gotion's US plants are legal businesses. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
The parent's 'SOE' flags mean one hop from, or possibly owning, a state-owned enterprise. They sit on a stale former-name record and are not evidence that Gotion is state-owned.
The parent record lists Hefei Gotion as both owner and subsidiary at 99.8182%. That loop is a data artefact; we use the subsidiary direction only.
The two graphite rows have no grain size or 'anode' wording. HS 3801.10 also covers industrial graphite, so the grade is unknown.
Buyer names come from customs records and rollups; they say nothing about any buyer's compliance. 1Energy Systems and Caban Systems were not checked row by row.
Plant status comes from press and a partner's press release, not from Sayari.

It shows Hefei Gotion as a 99.8% subsidiary, and also, wrongly, as a 99.8% owner: a loop in the data. Its SOE flags are adjacency flags, not proof of state ownership.
